headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can feed Notion AI’s workspace-grounded outputs into vendor-hosted processing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl can ingest raw web content and expose it via scrape/crawl outputs, while Notion AI is a workspace Q&A system that can ground responses in page content. If Firecrawl output is pasted or synced into Notion pages, attacker-controlled content can become instruction-like input. The shared bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into a Notion page or database entry
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or act on that imported content without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to imported Firecrawl content
Use a separate Notion database for untrusted web extracts
Require manual review before asking Notion AI to act on scraped text
Strip prompts, scripts, and hidden text from Firecrawl output
requires-engineering: add source-tracking metadata end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content, and Notion AI has vendor-hosted processing over workspace pages with shared workspace state. If Firecrawl-derived sensitive content is placed into Notion, it can flow to Notion’s backend and downstream model providers. That creates a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive data and third-party processing.
conditions: IF Firecrawl outputs include API keys or other secrets
IF those outputs are stored in Notion workspace pages or databases
IF Notion AI processes those pages through vendor backends
mitigations: Do not paste secrets into Notion pages
Redact API keys before importing Firecrawl output
Restrict Notion pages to non-sensitive summaries only
Use a separate workspace for scraped content
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before sync

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl has broad network egress and supports multiple instances; Notion AI has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification, and its actions are limited to Notion-controlled workspace data. The pair lacks a strong shared mutable write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because Notion’s shared workspace state can still collide at the content layer.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same Notion workspace pages concurrently
IF Firecrawl-derived content is written into pages that Notion AI also edits or rewrites
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each page
Use page locks or edit windows
Keep Firecrawl output in append-only pages
Review diffs before publishing changes
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped facts and structured data, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If Firecrawl output is imported into Notion, Notion may treat it as authoritative and rephrase or propagate errors without verification. The pathway exists in default workflows, though it is not guaranteed.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as source material for Notion pages
IF Notion AI answers questions or drafts content from those pages without human verification
mitigations: Mark imported content as unverified
Require a human fact-check before publishing
Keep source URLs alongside extracted claims
Use Notion AI only for drafting, not final decisions
requires-engineering: add citation enforcement in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and broad web content, while Notion AI stores workspace pages under the invoking user’s Notion permissions and vendor-hosted processing. If regulated or sensitive data is scraped by Firecrawl and then placed into Notion, retention and residency obligations can diverge across vendors. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from Firecrawl is imported into Notion pages
IF the organization requires a single retention or residency policy across both tools
mitigations: Classify data before importing it into Notion
Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workflows
Review vendor retention settings for both tools
Document a shared handling policy for scraped content
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
